kept.q: Calculate the number of moles of sodium hydroxide, NaOH, present in 20 g of the compound. [Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1]
kept.explanation: Molar mass of NaOH = 23 + 16 + 1 = 40 g/mol. Number of moles = mass/molar mass = 20/40 = 0.5 mol.
kept.pidgin: Molar mass of NaOH na 23+16+1 = 40 g/mol. Moles = mass over molar mass = 20/40 = 0.5 mol.

kept.q: What is the mass of 0.25 mole of calcium trioxocarbonate(IV), CaCO3? [Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16]
kept.explanation: Molar mass of CaCO3 = 40 + 12 + (16x3) = 100 g/mol. Mass = moles x molar mass = 0.25 x 100 = 25 g.
kept.pidgin: Molar mass of CaCO3 na 40+12+(16x3) = 100 g/mol. Mass = moles x molar mass = 0.25 x 100 = 25 g.

kept.q: Calculate the number of molecules present in 4.4 g of carbon(IV) oxide, CO2. [C = 12, O = 16, Avogadro's number = 6.02 x 10^23 mol^-1]
kept.explanation: Molar mass of CO2 = 12 + (16x2) = 44 g/mol. Moles = 4.4/44 = 0.1 mol. Number of molecules = 0.1 x 6.02x10^23 = 6.02x10^22 molecules.
kept.pidgin: Molar mass of CO2 na 12+(16x2) = 44 g/mol. Moles = 4.4/44 = 0.1 mol. Number of molecules = 0.1 x 6.02x10^23 = 6.02x10^22 molecules.

kept.q: What volume, at standard temperature and pressure (s.t.p), will be occupied by 0.2 mole of oxygen gas, O2? [Molar volume of a gas at s.t.p = 22.4 dm3/mol]
kept.explanation: Volume = number of moles x molar volume = 0.2 x 22.4 dm3/mol = 4.48 dm3.
kept.pidgin: Volume = number of moles x molar volume = 0.2 x 22.4 dm3/mol = 4.48 dm3.

kept.q: Magnesium reacts with excess hydrochloric acid according to the equation: Mg + 2HCl -> MgCl2 + H2. If 3.0 g of magnesium reacts completely with excess acid, calculate the volume of hydrogen gas produced at s.t.p. [Mg = 24, Molar volume of a gas at s.t.p = 22.4 dm3/mol]
kept.explanation: Moles of Mg = 3.0/24 = 0.125 mol. From the equation, 1 mole Mg produces 1 mole H2, so moles of H2 = 0.125 mol. Volume of H2 = 0.125 x 22.4 = 2.8 dm3.
kept.pidgin: Moles of Mg = 3.0/24 = 0.125 mol. From the equation, 1 mole Mg go give 1 mole H2, so moles of H2 = 0.125 mol. Volume of H2 = 0.125 x 22.4 = 2.8 dm3.

kept.q: A compound was found to contain, by mass, 40% carbon, 6.7% hydrogen and 53.3% oxygen. Determine the empirical formula of the compound. [C = 12, H = 1, O = 16]
kept.explanation: Divide each percentage by its atomic mass: C = 40/12 = 3.33, H = 6.7/1 = 6.7, O = 53.3/16 = 3.33. Dividing by the smallest value (3.33) gives C:H:O = 1:2:1, so the empirical formula is CH2O.
